title: Taskified admin 'Swiftlets' — contextual runbooks surfaced as micro-operators
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
Ship a lightweight, embeddable surface for converting canonical runbooks into 'Swiftlets' — tiny, opinionated admin operators that can be executed from the Console, CLI, or support chat. Swiftlets are intended for first-line support and automated remediation flows: they must be idempotent, permission-gated, and instrumented for cost/latency impact.

Goals:
- Provide a composable runtime for taskified runbooks with typed inputs, dry-run, and safe rollback hooks.
- Surface Swiftlets contextually (route, model, customer tier) so support can run the exact remediation for an incident without copying scripts.
- Enforce RBAC + approval gates. Integrate KMS audit headers for Private deployments.
- Emit telemetry (attempts, success, token-cost estimate, error classes) to the ops dashboard and SLO telemetry.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Large-scale cataloging UI (that will be a follow-up PM ticket).
- Full marketplace or cross-tenant sharing.

Design/Implementation notes:
1) Runtime: extend the existing runbook task runner to accept 'swiftlet' manifest (YAML). A swiftlet contains metadata, typed params, a dry-run adaptor and a handler reference (shelllet, python snippet, or call to admin-api).
2) Safety model: each swiftlet requires a manifest field 'effects: none|read|mutate' and 'approval_required: true|false'. Mutation swiftlets must be run with an escalation token (timebound) and logged to audit.
3) Execution paths: Console button -> opens param modal with prefilled context -> dry-run summary -> request approval if needed -> execute. CLI: rust binary extension that validates manifest locally then hits admin-exec service. Support Chat: a controlled conversational flow that proposes applicable swiftlets and runs after explicit confirmation.
4) Observability: add a SwiftletExecution event with fields (swiftlet_id, user, team, params_hash, cost_estimate, duration_ms, status_code, error_class). Wire to Ops-Events (existing pipeline).
5) Rollout: start with three low-risk swiftlets (reindex embeddings cache, rotate a non-critical API key, bump tracing sample rate) in sandbox, then a canary group of support engineers, then wide release.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Embedding arbitrary scripts vs manifest-only handlers: we favor handler refs to limit blast radius and enable static analysis.
- Client-side dry-run complexity vs server-side simulation: we will do server-side dry-run summaries to avoid leaking infra details to clients.
- Approval UX: single-approver vs multi-approver. Start single-approver with audit trail; expand later for high-sensitivity ops.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Swiftlet manifest schema and validation (json-schema).
- Server-side executor extension with RBAC checks, approval gate, and audit emission.
- Console modal flow + CLI shim to execute swiftlets (minimal UI).
- Telemetry events and a basic dashboard tile in Console: last 7 days swiftlet success/failure and cost estimates.

Success criteria:
- Support team can run 3 canonical swiftlets end-to-end in sandbox with dry-run and execution logs.
- No security findings in initial review.
- Telemetry shows events for each execution and token-cost estimates within 10% of actual billed tokens.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Manifest schema published in Confluence and validated by unit tests. 2) Three canary swiftlets fully functional in sandbox. 3) Approval gating and RBAC enforced end-to-end. 4) SwiftletExecution telemetry flowing to Ops dashboard with correct fields. 5) Security sign-off (security_review_required:true).
comments: 2025-02-18 - Ava Martinez: Created initial spec and prototype manifest. Attached Confluence design. Marking as P1 because this unlocks faster incident remediation and reduces MTTR.

2025-02-20 - Engineering kickoff (Ravi): Architecture spike completed. Decided to implement handler refs rather than arbitrary scripts to simplify static permission checks. Prototype executor accepts shell handler and lambda reference.
2025-02-24 - Design review (Leah Kim): Console modal mockups reviewed. UX asks for clearer dry-run diff and provenance link. Added 'open in terminal' quick copy button to modal.

2025-02-26 - Security (Marcus): High-level review done. Two items: (1) require KMS envelope for escalation tokens; (2) ensure audit events are immutable. Security will run a follow-up review for Private deployments.
2025-03-01 - QA (Jordan): Dry-run harness tests pass for two swiftlets; third one flaky in sandbox due to order-of-operations race. Investigating executor idempotency semantics.

2025-03-03 - Ravi Patel: Implemented telemetry event and basic dashboard tile. Filed minor follow-up ENG-426427 for idempotency patch and ENG-426428 for multi-approver enhancement. Ready for limited canary on 2025-03-05.
